perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s subjective perspective, he has access to:

- I am Harold Padilla, a project manager. Arthur Begum is a police officer and a friend I rely on for advice. We met at a coffee shop.
- I felt frustrated and anxious because my project team seemed unmotivated and it was affecting progress. I told Arthur I was at my wit’s end.
- Arthur told me motivation can be tricky, that I should understand what drives each team member individually, and that one-on-one conversations could help people feel valued and understood personally.
- I admitted I had not tried that, said I would, and felt more hopeful.
- I decided to implement Arthur’s advice. In a team meeting, I proposed quick one-on-one chats to learn what motivates each person. Team Member 1 said that could be helpful. Team Member 2 said they were open to it. I said I would schedule time with each of them.
- Later, I noticed the team still was not responding well. I felt disappointed and worried, and I told Arthur that his suggestions had not worked and I feared for the project.
- Arthur told me there might be deeper issues: personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors. He said I might need to dig deeper. I agreed and planned another round of meetings.
- I held one-on-one meetings and asked team members about concerns or problems. Team Member 1 told me there was tension between a few people affecting work. Team Member 2 told me they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, which hurt motivation. I said I would look into resolving conflicts, consider redistributing tasks, and cared about their well-being.
- I felt optimistic and empowered, believing that addressing individual concerns would improve performance. I decided to create a more supportive, open environment with regular feedback sessions and team-building activities.
- I announced these changes to the team. Team Member 1 said it sounded great and would help. Team Member 2 agreed and said it was good that concerns were being addressed. I said I was glad and that their input and well-being were crucial.

I do not know hidden causes, private thoughts, or events beyond what I directly observed, heard, said, or decided.
